title.rendered: Huerfano County Lifts Stage One Fire Restrictions

content.rendered:
On October 13, 2026; the Huerfano County Board of County Commissioners (BOCC) voted to lift Stage One Fire Restrictions. This followed decisions by Pueblo & Custer Counties and the USFS-Pike-San Isabel National Forest to lift Stage One Fire Restrictions due to seasonal weather and increased moisture and was recommended by the chiefs of Upper Huerfano Fire Protection District, Huerfano County Fire Protection District, and La Veta Fire Protection District as well as Huerfano County Emergency Management.

Huerfano County Emergency Management encourages responsible fire use, and reminds the public to follow the County’s Burn Permit process.

Earlier this year, on March 31st, 2026; by order of the BOCC, Huerfano County moved into Stage 1 Fire Restrictions. On June 30, 2026, by order of the BOCC, Huerfano County moved into Stage 2 Fire Restrictions. On August 25, 2026, the Stage 2 Fire Restrictions were lowered back to Stage One.

As of October 13, 2026; Huerfano County is no longer in Fire Restrictions.

By order of the Huerfano County Board of Commissioners, Huerfano County has been placed under Stage 1 Fire Restrictions effective August 25, 2026.

The following activities are prohibited during Stage 1 Fire Restrictions:

  1. Building, maintaining, attending or using a fire or campfire except within fire grates in developed/improved campgrounds and picnic grounds or private residences in areas cleared at least six feet of all flammable materials. Rock campfire rings and fire pans are considered temporary and are not acceptable. Devices using gas, jellied petroleum, or pressurized liquid fuel are permitted.
  2. Smoking, except within an enclosed vehicle or building, a developed recreation site or while stopped in an area at least three feet in diameter that is barren or cleared of all flammable materials.
  3. Possessing, discharging or using any type of fireworks or other pyrotechnic device to include sparklers. This does not differentiate between lawful use and careless/negligent use of fireworks, but prohibits all fireworks activity and use on public and private lands.
  4. Operating a chainsaw without a USDA or SAE approved spark arrester properly installed and working, a chemical fire extinguisher of not less than eight ounces capacity by weight, and one round point shovel with an overall length of at least 36 inches.
  5. Using an explosive or exploding targets.
  6. Using a welder, either arc or gas, or operating acetylene or other torch with open flame, except in cleared areas of at least ten feet in diameter with a chemical pressurized fire extinguisher of not less than eight ounces capacity.

The following exceptions are permitted during Stage 1 Fire Restrictions:

  1. Open burning conducted with an approved open burning permit.
  2. Smokeless flares or safety flares for the combustion of waste gasses.
  3. Flares used to indicate danger.
  4. All prescribed burns will be reviewed and approved by a qualified representative from the respective fire district.

These restrictions are in place until rescinded by the Board of County Commissioners.  Violations are punishable by a fine of up to $1000.  Anyone negligently or willfully starting a wildland fire could also be held responsible for the costs of that fire.

Additional information on Huerfano County’s Burn Ordinance, including fire restriction definitions, can be found in the Huerfano County Code, Article II of Chapter 10.

The Aspen Acres Fire has caused evacuations of Rye, Beulah, Wetmore, Colorado City, and other areas. There are some residents of Huerfano County who access their properties through Colorado City. This area is currently under Mandatory Evacuation until further notice.

Pre-Evacuation means to prepare essential items at this time and ensure your emergency kits are in or near your primary vehicle. Include the 6 Ps: People/Pets, Papers (documents), Prescriptions, Pictures, Personal Computers, and Plastic/Cash. Additional notices with guidance will be sent via HCNotify and Huerfano Emergency Management if an evacuation is ordered. A map of the area will be shared to social media and is on this page.

Please register for emergency alerts through HCNotify https://huerfano.us/hcnotify-sign-up/

August 4, 2026 11:30AM Update

As of 11:30AM today, all Huerfano County zones still in Pre-Evacuation have now been cleared from any level of evacuation status. Re-entry cards are no longer required in H-1, H-16, or H-17. 

Thank you to all personnel responding to the Aspen Acres incident who have kept our communities safe. Huerfano County Government is deeply grateful for your service.

July 23, 2026 8:30AM Update

As of 8AM today, all three of Huerfano County’s Mandatory Evacuation Zones – H-1, H-16, and H-17 – have now moved to Pre-Evacuation Status. H-15 has been cleared from Pre-Evacuation status.
Residents are free to return to their properties in all Huerfano County zones impacted by the Aspen Acres Fire. Residents who do not have re-entry cards are able to get them at the Huerfano County Department of Human Services building at 121 W 6th Street in Walsenburg from 10AM to 5PM Monday-Thursday and tomorrow, Friday 7/24 from 12PM-5PM at the Huerfano County Community Center in Walsenburg (928 S Russell Street).
As a reminder, Pre-Evacuation Status does mean to still be prepared to leave in the event the situation changes for the worse.
An updated map will be released as soon as it is available and added to this post.

July 21, 2026 1:30PM Update

H-1, H-16, and H-17 remain in Mandatory Evacuation status due to active fire activity in or near those zones. Displaced residents who have not already done so should go to the Huerfano County Department of Human Services – located at 121 W 6th Street in Walsenburg – between the hours of 10AM-5PM to obtain reentry cards. These cards will be necessary to go back in the zones when they are downgraded from Mandatory Evacuation. 

On Friday night, July 17, the Huerfano County Sheriff’s Office released a statement about the community of Libre and its evacuation status. While Libre was not part of the original H-16 and H-17 mandatory evacuation, a field decision was made to include it out of an abundance of caution given changing fire conditions and later downgraded from mandatory evacuation to pre-evacuation. 

Huerfano County residents displaced by the Aspen Acres Fire are also able to make use of resources available at the Recovery Assistance Center – located at Beulah Heights Elementary, 2670 Delphinium Street, Pueblo – Monday through Friday from 12PM-6PM. Behavioral health, human services, food distribution, and other resources are available through the Center.

Huerfano County Government continues to work closely with the Northern Rockies IMT in command of the Aspen Acres Fire and will provide updates as they become available.

July 16, 2026 2:30PM Update

Huerfano County Government and the Northern Rockies IMT will be hosting a community meeting in Gardner tomorrow evening at 7PM. This meeting will also be streamed online.

Location: Raymond Aguirre Community Center 28 Co Rd 632 Gardner, CO 81040

When: Friday, July 17 from 7PM-8PM

July 14, 2026 10:30PM Update

Huerfano County has three defined mandatory evacuation zones as of July 14, 2026 due to the ongoing Aspen Acres Fire. Those zones are located in the Bartlett Trail Subdivision Area (referred to as H-1 in Aspen Acres mapping) and on National Forest Service land with private inholdings in Zones H-16 and H-17. 

H-1 remains under Mandatory Evacuation due to ongoing fire activity near that zone and the Pueblo County zone north of H-1, which has the primary ingress/egress route for H-1.

H-16 and H-17 reflect National Forest Service land with private inholdings East of Williams Creek at the National Forest border, following Williams Creek North to where it intersects with CR 630, following CR 630 generally north to the intersection with CR 636, following CR 630 West to where it intersects with CR 634 (Gardner Road) and then running due North to the County Line. Southern and Eastern boundaries of these zones are the US Forest Service boundary and the Northern boundary is the County Line. 

For additional clarification; County residents who live west of Santana Butte and Badito Cone and off of Forest Service land are NOT under Mandatory Evacuation and remain under a Fire/Smoke Advisory. This Mandatory Evacuation is intended for National Forest Service boundaries and those residents who live on private land within those boundaries.

Additional updates will be shared on Wednesday, July 15. A Community Meeting with Incident Management Team (IMT) support in Gardner will be scheduled in the near future after the transition from the Alaska IMT to the Northern Rockies IMT. 

July 14, 2026 11AM Update

The Huerfano County Sheriff’s Office is evacuating all areas within the US Forest Service to the East of where Williams Creek crosses into the National Forest and then following Williams Creek North to where Williams Creek intersects with CR 630 and following CR 630 generally north to where CR 630 intersects with CR 636 and continuing to follow CR 630 west to where it intersects with CR 634 (Gardner Road) and then running due North to the County Line.  Southern and Eastern boundaries of the evacuation zone are the US Forest Service boundary and the Northern boundary is the County Line.

July 13, 2026 4PM Update

Huerfano County Sheriff’s Office is placing all Forest Service land North of CO-69 to the northern-most Huerfano County line under Pre-Evacuation Notice. This includes CR 630 North of CR 630.1 and CR 634 North of 634.2, as well as the entirety of the Greenhorn Wilderness Area.

Please prepare essential items and ensure your emergency kits are in or near your primary vehicle. Include the 6 P’s: People/Pets, Papers, Prescriptions, Pictures, Personal Computers, and Plastic or Cash. Additional notices will be sent via HCNotify, posted on the County website and shared to the County Facebook.

The previous mandatory evacuation zone – the Bartlett Trail Subdivision, shown to the east on the attached map – remains under mandatory evacuation until further notice.

July 10, 2026 3:30PM Update

The Bartlett Trail Subdivision area remains under mandatory evacuation per direction from the Alaska Incident Management Team working the Aspen Acres Fire. This is due to ongoing fire activity in the vicinity and weather conditions with high fire danger.

Huerfano residents impacted by this evacuation order can obtain reentry cards at the Pueblo Disaster Assistance Center, which is currently open from 9AM to 6PM through July 14. Residents are encouraged to get their reentry cards before the evacuation order is lifted. We will continue to post updates on the Disaster Assistance Center schedule beyond July 14 once we have that information. The Disaster Assistance Center also contains resources for food, basic needs, mental and behavioral health, and more for those displaced by the Aspen Acres Fire.

The Alaska Incident Management Team continues to actively work on the Aspen Acres Fire and has open communication channels with Huerfano County Government and the Huerfano County Sheriff’s Office. Huerfano County will continue to share the daily updates from the Alaska team on the County Facebook Page and will post additional updates as they impact Huerfano County.

July 5, 2026 3:30PM Update

Huerfano County has extended the Fire and Smoke Advisory from this morning as far east as I-25. The advisory area now includes areas north of Highway 69 from the Custer County Line following CO-69 to the intersection with Red Rock Road, east to I-25, and follows I-25 north to the Pueblo County Line. 

A fire advisory is one level below a Pre-Evacuation and is to give residents advance notice of the potential for their area to be placed on pre-evacuation or mandatory evacuation. The Bartlett Trail Subdivision area remains under mandatory evacuation. Evacuees from this area seeking additional information should contact the Pueblo Disaster Assistance Center. Their hours and contact information are available at https://mars.colorado.gov/DAC

The next planned update from Huerfano County will be tomorrow morning. Please follow the Aspen Acres Fire 2026 Facebook page for updates from the Alaska Incident Management Team.

July 5, 2026 10:30AM Update

New Fire and Smoke Advisory for Aspen Acres Fire

Out of an abundance of caution, a Fire and Smoke Advisory is now in effect for the Upper Huerfano and Gardner area.  The advisory, which has been coordinated with Custer County, includes areas north of Highway 69 from the Custer County Line following CO-69 to Badito (CO-69 and CR 616), and then north along the eastern edge of the Greenhorn Mountain Wilderness to the Pueblo County Line. This extends the Fire and Smoke Advisory Area announced yesterday (7/4) by Custer County for Southern Custer County east of Colorado Highway 69 and south of Rosita Road to the Huerfano County Line.

A fire advisory is one level below a Pre-Evacuation and is to give residents advance notice of the potential for their area to be placed on pre-evacuation or mandatory evacuation.

Big Sheep Fire Pre-Evacuation Lifted

The Pre-Evacuation Notice for Big Sheep Fire south of Highway 69 in Huerfano County has been lifted.

July 4, 2026 1PM Update

Below are updates from the Alaska IMT Public Information Team.  One area of Huerfano County remains under mandatory evacuation.  Alaska IMT and the County continue to monitor the fire and the creation of additional pre-evacuation zones within Huerfano County is a possibility.  No decisions have been made as of this posting. An update will be posted later this evening or earlier if the need arises.

July 4 Alaska IMT Daily Update

July 4 Alaska IMT Updated Map

July 4 Alaska IMT Smoke Outlook

Huerfano County remains on Stage 2 Fire Restrictions.  Fireworks are prohibited throughout the County.

July 3, 2026 7PM Update

Huerfano County Sheriff’s Office is en route now to the Aspen Acres pre-evacuation zone. At this time it is a mandatory evacuation north towards Pueblo’s Disaster Assistance Center. This is a rapidly evolving situation and the evacuation is in place before access may become compromised. Additional information available at https://mars.colorado.gov/DAC

July 3, 2026 1PM Update

Aspen Acres Fire is a rapidly evolving situation – please review the updated Overview section. At this time the pre-evacuation notice for Huerfano County near Rye remains in effect and the area is unchanged from previous updates. The Huerfano County Sheriff’s Office and Emergency Management continue to monitor the situation and any updates will be released as quickly as possible in conjunction with Alaska IMT and Pueblo County Sheriff’s Office.

July 2, 2026 12PM Update

The pre-evacuation notice remains in effect for areas of Huerfano County that would have to evacuate through Colorado City due to the Aspen Acres Fire. If you are between the eastern boundary of national forest land and the intersection between CR 670 and CR 660 by Apache City (West of I-25), you are within the affected region. Additional updates will be provided as the situation evolves.

July 1, 2026 7PM Update

Shaded area is under pre-evacuation notice

The previously-alerted area – see above map image – remains under Pre-Evacuation until further notice. At this time, expanded Pre-Evacuation notices in Huerfano County are not anticipated, but please be aware that this is an evolving situation.

Guidance on where to go in the case of an evacuation will be shared if and when that decision is made.

Please continue to report any sightings of flame to 911; smoke calls can be directed to Huerfano County Dispatch Non-Emergency at 719-738-1044. Huerfano County Emergency Services will continue monitoring the situation and provide updates as soon as possible if the situation changes.

July 1, 2026 4:30PM Update

Huerfano County Sheriff’s Office is putting areas of Huerfano County that would have to utilize Colorado City evacuation routes on Pre-Evacuation due to the Aspen Acres Fire. Please prepare essential items at this time and ensure your emergency kits are in or near your primary vehicle. Include the 6 P’s: People/Pets, Papers (documents), Prescriptions, Pictures, Personal Computers, and Plastic/Cash. Additional notices with guidance will be sent via HCNotify and Huerfano Emergency Management if an evacuation is ordered.

Please register for emergency alerts through HCNotify https://huerfano.us/hcnotify-sign-up/ – additional updates will be released as quickly as possible.

By order of the Huerfano County Board of Commissioners, Huerfano County has been placed under Stage 2 Fire Restrictions effective June 30, 2026. Stage 2 restrictions incorporate and expand upon the earlier Stage 1 restrictions.

The following activities are prohibited on all public and private lands, roads, and trails within Huerfano County:

  1. Building, maintaining, attending, or using any fire or campfire.
    • Exception:
  2. Discharging, or using any type of fireworks or other pyrotechnic device, including sparklers. All fireworks activity and use is prohibited on public and private lands, whether lawful or careless/negligent.
  3. Trash or refuse burning of any kind, even in burn barrels with approved screening.
  4. Smoking, except within an enclosed vehicle or building, a barren area, a developed recreation site, or on a paved surface at least three feet in diameter.
  5. Operating a chainsaw or any motorized equipment for any purpose other than fire mitigation work. Mitigation equipment must be on hand for each person operating such equipment (for example, a chemical fire extinguisher, shovels, and a spark arrester). You must call Huerfano County Dispatch at 719-738-1044 with the start time, end time, and location of the activity.
  6. Blasting, welding, or operating any torch with an open flame, or other activities that generate flame or flammable material. You must call Huerfano County Dispatch at 719-738-1044 with the start time, end time, and location of the activity.
  7. Using explosives or exploding targets.

The following exceptions are permitted:

  1. Propane grills are allowed if the grill can be turned off with a knob or the flip of a switch.
  2. If fire is a requirement to do business (for example, a barbecue restaurant), the business shall be requested to meet mitigation guidelines commensurate with the size and location of the fire and the level of fire restriction enacted.
  3. Open burning conducted with an approved open burning permit.
  4. Smokeless flares or safety flares for the combustion of waste gasses.
  5. Flares used to indicate danger.
  6. Prescribed burns reviewed and approved by a qualified representative from the respective fire district.

These restrictions are in place until rescinded by the Board of County Commissioners. Violations are punishable by a fine of up to $1000. Anyone negligently or willfully starting a wildland fire could also be held responsible for the costs of that fire.

Additional information on Huerfano County’s Burn Ordinance, including fire restriction definitions, can be found in the Huerfano County Code, Article II of Chapter 10.

Information on restrictions in other Counties and on Federal Lands in Colorado are available from the Colorado Department of Homeland Security and Emergency Management.

Overview

There is an active wildfire in Huerfano County South and West of Big Sheep Mountain near County Road 531. Multiple Fire Protection Districts and the Huerfano County Fire Protection District are responding.

No evacuations have been ordered at this time. The pre-evacuation notice has been lifted.

This page will only be updated if there is a significant change.

Register for HCNotify alerts at https://huerfano.us/hcnotify-sign-up/

July 6, 2026 Update

At 6AM this morning the State Incident Management Team returned the Big Sheep (aka Sheep Head) Fire to local control. The fire is 100% contained and the last measurement of the size of the fire was 1,322 acres.

This will be the last planned update for the Big Sheep Fire. Updates will only be posted if there is a significant change.

July 4, 2026 Big Sheep Daily Update

July 3, 2026 10:30AM Update

Please see the below two links for the State Incident Management Team’s Big Sheep (AKA Sheep Head) Fire morning update. One is an updated map of the fire and the other is their Daily Update.

Updated Big Sheep Fire Map

July 3, 2026 Big Sheep Daily Update

The next planned update will be tomorrow morning.

July 2, 2026, 9PM Update

Big Sheep Fire grew to 1281 acres today as a result of controlled burn operations and remains at 50% containment. Due to ongoing Red Flag Warning weather conditions, the Pre-Evacuation Notice will remain in effect. The next update will be after 8AM tomorrow.

July 2, 2026, 11AM Update

Big Sheep Fire operations continue today; the fire remains at 50% containment and 1153 acres. A Colorado State Incident Management Team (IMT) will be taking over operations today and the public messaging cadence may be adjusted based on direction from the IMT. Given relative humidity and Red Flag Warning weather conditions today, the Pre-Evacuation Notice will remain in effect.

July 1, 2026 – 8PM Update

Big Sheep Fire containment remains at 50% due to controlled burnout operations designed to prevent larger expansion. Overall size is 1153 acres. The pre-evacuation notice will remain in effect given the possibility of changing conditions and will be re-evaluated again at the end of daily operations tomorrow. San Isabel Electric has confirmed that all meters impacted by the Big Sheep Fire have been restored to active service. The next planned update will be 10AM Thursday, 7/2.

July 1, 2026 – 11AM Update

Incident Command of the Big Sheep Fire has been released from the La Veta Fire Protection District to the Colorado Division of Fire Prevention and Control. Local units will continue to provide assistance with support from Huerfano County Emergency Management and the Huerfano County Sheriff’s Office.

There are still a few meters without power. San Isabel Electric is working to restore service as soon as possible today. The focus of today’s operations is on two primary hotspots as well as minimizing additional flare-ups. The pre-evacuation notice will be re-evaluated after operations today.

The Board of County Commissioners, Elected Officials and Staff of Huerfano County would like to extend our sincere gratitude to all of the volunteers and crews from local, state, and federal agencies who have worked around the clock on the Big Sheep Fire and other wildfires in the region over the last several weeks.  Some of these volunteers and crews have come from as far as Boise, Idaho. Your dedication to all of our communities and public service are deeply appreciated! 

The next planned update for the Big Sheep Fire will be later this afternoon.

June 30, 2026 – 8PM Update

Fire operations utilizing local, state, and federal resources have achieved 50% containment on the Big Sheep Fire, and will monitor hot spots and flare ups overnight and tomorrow.

At this time the pre-evacuation notice does remain in effect through the end of day tomorrow, unless the situation improves. There are a few residences still without power. San Isabel Electric Association and Incident Command are working to restore power once it is safe to do so.

No structures have been lost and the overall size of the fire is roughly 1100 acres. The next planned update will be around 9AM tomorrow morning.

June 30, 2026 – 2PM Update

Fire suppression and containment activities continue on the Big Sheep Fire. A helicopter team from Colorado Division of Fire Prevention and Control has provided aerial assistance while additional ground units are working on containment and hot spots.
The pre-evacuation notice will remain in place through 6PM today and will be re-evaluated based on afternoon operations and weather conditions. Thunderstorms are expected in the vicinity this afternoon to the early evening that may impact operations.
Huerfano County is now under Stage 2 Fire Restrictions; more information on these restrictions will be shared separately. The next planned update will be after 6PM tonight.

June 30, 2026 – 9AM Update

The Big Sheep fire expanded up to 1000 acres, with 30% containment. Overnight burnout operations were successful at directing the course of the fire. Additional resources are en route to work on hot spots and increased containment. No evacuation notices have been issued. However, the pre-evacuation notice does currently remain in effect but will be re-evaluated after 12 Noon today. The cause of the fire has not yet been determined.

Huerfano County would like to thank La Veta Fire, Huerfano Fire, Upper Huerfano Fire, Costilla County, Colorado Division of Fire Prevention and Control, and the federal Bureau of Land Management for their efforts on scene. We are also grateful for law enforcement personnel from the Sheriff’s Office and Walsenburg Police Department who are providing direct communication with impacted residents and scene security.

June 29, 2026 – 10PM Update

At this time, no evacuation notices have been issued and no evacuation notices are anticipated overnight.

The pre-evacuation notice remains in effect out of an abundance of caution and was sent to a larger area than where any potential evacuations would occur; as far west as CR 562, east to Farisita (CR 540 & CR 546), and north to Highway 69. If an evacuation were ordered, a formal map would be shared.

Fire containment, suppression, and monitoring activities are continuing overnight. An update is planned for Tuesday morning barring any urgent changes. Huerfano County Emergency Management will continue to monitor the fire and will issue a Reverse 911 alert via HCNotify and update the County website and social media.

Register for HCNotify alerts at https://huerfano.us/hcnotify-sign-up/

If you are in the impacted area and see spreading flames or spot fires overnight, please call 911 to inform Dispatch.

June 29, 2026 – 8PM Update

Pre-Evacuation Notice

This is a pre-evacuation notice for areas north of the Big Sheep Fire to Highway 69 exposed to the smoke. Please prepare essential items at this time and ensure your emergency kits are in or near your primary vehicle. Include the 6 Ps: People/Pets, Papers (documents), Prescriptions, Pictures, Personal Computers, and Plastic/Cash. Responders are actively engaging with the fire and working on containment. Additional notices will be sent if an evacuation is ordered.

The current estimate for the size of the fire is 315-340 acres.

After a discussion with necessary stakeholders, including all Fire District Chiefs, Huerfano County Sheriff Bruce Newman has lifted the Stage 1 Fire Restrictions as of May 27, 2022.

Please be advised that any requirements for your district regarding permits must be followed and dispatch must be notified of your burn. Even with the moisture received, we are asking all Huerfano County residents and tourists to remain diligent when conducting any type of fire, controlled or not.
